topic: AI Codebase Maturity Model: From Assisted Coding to Fully Autonomous Development

competitors.title: The AI Codebase Maturity Model: From Assisted Coding to Fully Autonomous Systems (ACMM)
key_points: 6-level framework (v2) describing how codebases evolve from basic AI-assisted coding to fully autonomous systems, inspired by CMMI
Each level defined by its feedback loop topology — specific mechanisms that must exist before next level becomes possible
Validated through 100-day experience report on KubeStellar Console (CNCF Kubernetes dashboard) built with Claude Code and GitHub Copilot
Central finding: intelligence resides in infrastructure of instructions, tests, metrics, and feedback loops, not in the AI model itself
Testing — volume of test cases, coverage thresholds, reliability of test execution — proved the single most important investment
Hive reference implementation: 74 CI/CD workflows, 32 nightly test suites, 91% code coverage, bug-to-fix times under 30 minutes 24/7
5x PR throughput and 37x issue throughput acceleration from Level 2 to Level 6
Cannot skip levels — each level requires another feedback mechanism to unlock the next

competitors.title: The AI Codebase Maturity Model: Mapping Five Levels of Agent Autonomy to Codex CLI
key_points: Maps each ACMM level to concrete Codex CLI configuration showing what to build at each stage
Level 0 (Spicy Autocomplete): AI suggests next line, human accepts/rejects — GitHub Copilot circa 2022
Level 1 (Coding Intern): Human delegates discrete tasks, AI handles assigned work, human remains system integrator
Level 2 (Junior Developer): AI handles multi-file changes, humans still review all code — most 'AI-native' teams operate here
Level 3 (Developer as Manager): Dynamic reverses — humans direct AI and review at feature/PR level; guardrails emerge
Level 4 (Developer as PM): Write specs, leave, verify test passage — code becomes opaque, evaluation focuses on outcomes
Level 5 (Dark Factory): Lights-out pipeline — humans own specifications, machines own implementation
Three-axis assessment: Autonomy (A), Controls (C), Governance (G) — each scored 0-5
Danger zone: high autonomy with weak controls (A3 but C1) invites silent failures
Navigation errors account for 27-52% of agent failures; explicit path guidance reduces navigation steps by 33-44%

competitors.title: AI Coding Maturity — Dark Factory (Shapiro Framework)
key_points: 6-level maturity model from autocomplete to autonomous software factory
Levels describe who does the work (human vs AI) and where human attention goes (code vs specs vs outcomes)
Not about tools — about engineering workflow and control systems
Higher levels require stronger controls; more AI autonomy without better gates is risk, not progress
Dark Factory = A5 + C5 + G5 — Level 5 on all three axes simultaneously
Key safeguard: holdout evaluation scenarios live outside the codebase — AI never sees test criteria
Digital twins simulate real services for full integration testing without production contact
Tiered target by risk class: Tier 1 (high risk) → A2-A3 with C3-C4; Tier 3 (low risk) → A4-A5 proving ground

competitors.title: AI Codebase Maturity Model: Feedback & Autonomy (Emergent Mind Analysis)
key_points: ACMM reframes maturity as emergent property of systemic telemetry, explicit instruction, and measurable trust boundaries
5-level framework (original v1): Assisted → Instructed → Measured → Adaptive → Self-Sustaining
33 distinct feedback loops control system behavior and quality in KubeStellar Console
81.4% PR acceptance overall, 99.7% of issues closed
Autonomous failure recovery: closed-loop workflows resolve incidents without human in the loop
Criticizes models conflating autonomy with maturity — distinguishes reckless delegation from measured system advancement
Code cleanliness and structure have direct, pronounced effect on AI agent acceptance rates and stability
Level 5 describes community-steered open source: community steers via issues, AI executes implementations
